key_insight: The paper replaces geometric coarse spaces in two-level overlapping Schwarz preconditioners with an algebraic multiscale coarse space built directly from the system matrix, preserving robustness for highly heterogeneous problems.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable, coefficient-aware preconditioning for elliptic diffusion and linear elasticity problems, especially when mesh geometry or coarse-space design is difficult to construct explicitly.
method: Build coarse basis functions from algebraic multiscale finite element ideas using only the system matrix.
Solve reduced boundary condition problems on interface slabs and extend them by energy-minimizing interpolation.
Embed the construction in an energy-minimizing framework so it applies to linear elasticity and unstructured decompositions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method is insensitive to increasing contrast for coarse-node inclusions, matches GDSW iteration counts in 3D log-normal diffusion while using a coarse problem about ten times smaller, and scales well for homogeneous linear elasticity.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well the interface-slabs and reduced boundary problems capture coefficient variation, and the fully algebraic elasticity variant omits rotational rigid-body-mode basis functions.
paper_title: An algebraic multiscale framework for two-level overlapping Schwarz preconditioners
